parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Surrey · Whalley and City Centre

Whalley is an MLS® area in North Surrey. The City says the Whalley community is in the northwest corner of Surrey, with the Fraser River on its north and west sides and much of its east edge on 144 Street. It surrounds City Centre. The name comes from Arthur Whalley, who settled near King George Boulevard and 108 Avenue in 1925. On the MLS® map, the Whalley area includes City Centre and runs from about 132 Street east to about 144 Street, and from about 96 Avenue north to near 108 Avenue.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and Surrey Schools.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

Whalley is an MLS® area name in Surrey. On the MLS® map it includes Surrey’s City Centre and King George Boulevard south of 108 Avenue. It runs from about 132 Street east to about 144 Street, with Guildford beyond, and from about 96 Avenue north to near 108 Avenue, with Bolivar Heights beyond. On 96 Avenue, Queen Mary Park is west of about 133 Street. These edges are approximate and are not an official City boundary, so ask me if a specific address is in it.
Three Expo Line stations serve the Whalley area: Gateway, Surrey Central and King George.
Surrey Central is the main bus exchange for the area. It is served by the R1 RapidBus, the
and many other routes, including the 314, 320, 321, 323, 324, 325, 326, 329, 335, 371, 373, 393, 501, 502, 503 and 509, plus the N19 NightBus. The 335, 371 and 373 also stop at Gateway Station.
The Surrey Langley SkyTrain will extend the Expo Line from King George Station along Fraser Highway to Langley. The Province expects it to open in late 2029.
Where does the name Whalley come from?
From Arthur Whalley, who settled near King George Boulevard and 108 Avenue in 1925, in an area then called Whalley’s Corner.
